chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sufyan from Dawud al-Raqqi who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Your breaking of the fast (Iftar) in the house of your Muslim brother is better than your fasting seventy or ninety times over.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for hosting Iftar for a Muslim brother according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that hosting a Muslim brother for Iftar yields a reward equivalent to fasting seventy or ninety times, a metric often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the reward of individual fasts rather than the entire month. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the communal and social dimensions of worship, elevating the act of strengthening familial and fraternal bonds through shared sustenance to a status nearly equal to prolonged personal devotion.
